note: KIMLA fibre-laser cutting machines as found on 2026-10-18 — the maker's own documents could not be retrieved (kimla.pl is denied by this environment's network policy); the figures below come from KIMLA's site as quoted by search and from dealers' used-machine listings. The machines are CUTTERS; the welding head of notebook 48 is a hypothetical configuration. Every scenario parameter marked 'assumed' is an engineering assumption with a range.

search_sources.what: a distributor's LF-series table: Finecut up to 6 kW, Flashcut up to 12 kW, Powercut up to 20 kW, Extremecut up to 30 kW; 'fiber lasers with efficiency above 30 %'
a used 2022 Powercut LF1020: 2 kW source, 2050 × 1050 mm sheet, 600 kg; supply 14 kW at 400 V 50 Hz; air 7 bar, nitrogen 30 bar, oxygen 10 bar
a used Powercut LF1530 6 kW: supply 12 kW at 400 V 50 Hz; 3050 × 1550 mm sheet, 900 kg
a used Powercut LF1530 4 kW: 3050 × 1550 mm, 900 kg
a distributor: laser power 2–12 kW, working width 1500–3000 mm, length 3000–12000 mm
a dealer: Finecut 1–2 kW (conflicts with 'up to 6 kW')

Powercut.note: 8 kW on KIMLA's LF page per one search result, 12 kW per another distributor, 20 kW per a third

conflicts: the Powercut tier's top power appears as 8, 12 and 20 kW across sources; the Finecut as 1–2 and 6 kW; the same 6 kW LF1530 is listed at 8.7 and 10 t and in two build years; the two listed supplies (14 kW for a 2 kW source, 12 kW for a 6 kW one) cannot both be the laser alone — the first must include the machine's drives and extraction; no cutting-thickness or cutting-speed table was found; the laser source's maker is not named ('efficiency above 30 %' is KIMLA's only figure). None of it is a welding specification.
hypothetical_welding_head: hypothetical: a welding head on the cutting gantry in place of the cutting head: collimator 100 mm, focusing 150–200 mm (Precitec ProCutter-class optics quoted for up to 30 kW by third parties, not tied to KIMLA), the process fibre of the power class, a shielding-gas nozzle instead of the cutting nozzle — nothing KIMLA offers

3 kW.basis: a 50 µm process fibre (the 3 kW class of notebook 47's WFL-3000)

6 kW.basis: a 100 µm process fibre (assumed: the usual 4–8 kW delivery)

12 kW.basis: a 100 µm fibre at a higher NA (assumed)

20 kW.basis: a 150 µm fibre (assumed: the 20 kW cutting class)

30 kW.basis: a 200 µm fibre (assumed: the 30 kW cutting class)

head.basis: assumed: ProCutter-class optics; the 200 mm focus is the nominal

optical_efficiency.basis: process fibre 0.2–0.5 dB and two lenses (notebook 47's ranges)

gas_flow_l_per_min.basis: assumed: argon (aluminium, stainless) or nitrogen (carbon steel) at a welding nozzle

gas_EUR_per_m3.basis: nitrogen from a generator or bulk (low) to argon cylinders (high; notebook 47's ECON)

max_feed_m_per_s.basis: assumed: a welding seam on a cutting gantry (the gantry cuts faster, the weld's tracking and gas coverage do not)

humping_m_per_s.basis: assumed: the humping/undercut onset of a narrow keyhole weld (literature's 5–15 m/min; a wobble raises it)

abs_keyhole_stainless.basis: assumed: as carbon steel, a little lower

reflectivity_carbon_steel.basis: a flat bare or molten steel surface at 1 µm

reflectivity_aluminium.basis: a flat aluminium surface at 1 µm

machine_capex_EUR.basis: assumed: a 1.5 × 3 m fibre cutting gantry with its enclosure, drives and controls (no KIMLA price found)

overheads_s.basis: assumed manual handling at a gantry; editable in the notebook

assembly_1m.note: an assembly with 1 m of weld in six seams
